name: Lemon Grove
seo_title: Christmas Events for Kids in Lemon Grove, CA 2026
seo_desc: Kids' Christmas in Lemon Grove, CA: the Community Bonfire at Treganza Heritage Park, Santa at the Lee House and holiday crafts at the library.
lede: Lemon Grove's biggest night of the holiday season is the city's Community Bonfire at Treganza Heritage Park, where families gather around the fire on Main Street and children visit Santa and his elves at the historic Lee House.
celebrates: Each December the City of Lemon Grove and the Lemon Grove Historical Society welcome the season with the Annual Community Bonfire at Treganza Heritage Park on Main Street. The city calls it the biggest event of the year: a live band, a Kids Zone, free cookies, hot chocolate and popcorn, and an official bonfire lighting at 6 pm. The historical society opens the Parsonage Museum and the Lee House, where children 10 and under can visit Santa and his elves. At the Lemon Grove Library on School Lane, Afterschool Adventures turn holiday themed in December, with wooden gingerbread houses, holiday loteria and popsicle stick ornaments.
lastyear: In 2025 the City of Lemon Grove held its 28th Annual Community Bonfire on Friday, December 5, from 4:30 to 8:30 pm at Treganza Heritage Park, 3200 Main Street. The city's posts promised the bonfire would go ahead rain or shine. The 2026 edition on Friday, December 4, is the 29th, again with the official bonfire lighting at 6 pm and Santa and his elves at the Lee House.
facts: Lemon Grove's landmark is a giant lemon. Designed by local architect Alberto O. Treganza, it was first built as a parade float for the 1928 Fourth of July Fiesta de San Diego parade, carrying the town's first Miss Lemon Grove, his 16 year old daughter Amorita. In 1930 the float was plastered into a permanent sculpture. Today the lemon weighs some 3,000 pounds, is about 10 feet long and sits at Broadway and Lemon Grove Avenue above the words Best Climate On Earth. Lemon Grove became California's 414th city on July 1, 1977.
trains: Lemon Grove sits right on the San Diego Trolley's Orange Line, with two stations in town: Massachusetts Avenue and Lemon Grove Depot. The depot station, near Broadway and Lemon Grove Avenue beside the Big Lemon, opened on May 12, 1989. Ride the Orange Line west to downtown San Diego and on to Balboa Park for the San Diego Model Railroad Museum, or drive out to Campo, where the Pacific Southwest Railway Museum runs the North Pole Limited, its most popular event, each holiday season.

traditions: The city lights a big bonfire at Treganza Heritage Park each December, with live music, a Kids Zone and free treats.
During the bonfire, children 10 and under can visit Santa and his elves inside the historical society's Lee House.
The Lemon Grove Historical Society opens its Parsonage Museum on bonfire night and sells a Parsonage Museum Christmas ornament.
Afterschool Adventures at the Lemon Grove Library turn to gingerbread houses, holiday loteria and ornaments in December.
The town's giant lemon sculpture at Broadway and Lemon Grove Avenue has stood near its current spot since 1930.
kidfact: Lemon Grove's giant lemon started out as a parade float in 1928. Today it weighs about 3,000 pounds and sits right beside the trolley tracks, above the words Best Climate On Earth.
faq: When is the Lemon Grove Community Bonfire?

The City of Lemon Grove holds its Annual Community Bonfire in early December at Treganza Heritage Park, 3200 Main Street. It runs in the evening, with the official bonfire lighting at 6 pm, live music, a Kids Zone and free cookies, hot chocolate and popcorn. The city says the event happens rain or shine.
Where can kids see Santa in Lemon Grove?

On bonfire night, the Lemon Grove Historical Society opens the Lee House at Treganza Heritage Park, and children 10 and under, accompanied by an adult, can visit Santa and his elves there. The historical society's Parsonage Museum is open the same evening, with Lemon Grove gifts and a Christmas ornament for sale.
Can I take the trolley to Lemon Grove's holiday events?

Yes. The San Diego Trolley's Orange Line stops at Lemon Grove Depot near Broadway and Lemon Grove Avenue, the corner where the Big Lemon stands. Treganza Heritage Park, home of the Community Bonfire, is at 3200 Main Street in downtown Lemon Grove, and the city's flyer notes that bikes and scooters are not permitted at the event.
What is the Big Lemon in Lemon Grove?

It is the town's landmark, a lemon sculpture about 10 feet long and weighing some 3,000 pounds at Broadway and Lemon Grove Avenue. Architect Alberto O. Treganza designed it as a parade float for 1928, and in 1930 it was plastered into a permanent sculpture above the words Best Climate On Earth.
